How Much Does 1800 GOT JUNK Cost in Jacksonville?

If you’re staring at a pile of old furniture, broken appliances, or a mountain of yard waste, the first question that pops into your mind is usually, “How much will this cost?” In Jacksonville, the answer isn’t a one‑size‑fits‑all number, but don’t worry—by the end of this guide you’ll know exactly what influences the price, what you can expect to pay, and how to lock in the best deal.

Understanding 1-800-GOT-JUNK?’s Pricing Model

Unlike many local haulers who charge by the hour or by the truckload, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? bases its pricing on three core factors:

  • Volume of junk: The amount of space your items take up in the truck.
  • Type of items: Heavy or hazardous materials may require special handling.
  • Location: How far the crew needs to travel within Jacksonville and surrounding areas.

This transparent, volume‑based approach means you only pay for what actually gets loaded onto the truck—no hidden fees, no surprise hourly rates.

Why Volume Matters More Than Weight

Think of the truck as a big box. The more items you can fit, the lower your cost per item. This is why a single couch might cost the same as a stack of cardboard boxes if they occupy the same cubic footage.

Key Factors That Influence the Cost in Jacksonville

1. Size of the Load

Most residential jobs in Jacksonville fall into one of three size categories:

  • Small (1‑2 rooms): $150‑$250
  • Medium (3‑4 rooms): $250‑$350
  • Large (5+ rooms or whole house): $350‑$500+

These are ballpark figures; your actual price will depend on how tightly the crew can pack the items.

2. Type of Items

Most household junk—furniture, mattresses, electronics, and yard waste—is standard. However, items like:

  • Hot tubs
  • Large appliances (refrigerators, washers)
  • Hazardous materials (paints, chemicals)

may incur a small surcharge because they require extra handling or disposal fees. The team will let you know before they start loading.

3. Accessibility and Travel Distance

Jacksonville’s sprawling layout means travel time can vary. If your property is tucked behind a narrow alley, on a second floor without an elevator, or far from the main road, the crew may need additional time to maneuver, which can add $20‑$40 to the final price.
